baseline_plan.title: Weight blanket edge with books
baseline_plan.summary: Drape the blanket over the chair seat and place a stack of books on the overhanging edge to hold it down using only weight.

steps.action: Drape the blanket over the office chair seat so that one edge extends beyond the seat.
steps.why_it_helps: Positions the blanket edge to be secured.

steps.action: Place the stack of books on the overhanging edge of the blanket to act as a weight.
steps.why_it_helps: The weight of the books prevents the blanket edge from shifting.

assumptions: The blanket is thick enough that the books will not slide off easily.
The books provide sufficient weight to hold the blanket edge in place.
The chair seat is flat and stable, allowing the blanket to lie smoothly.
unresolved_risks: If the blanket surface is very smooth, the books may still slide off.
If the books are too light, the edge may still shift under minor disturbances.
constraint_check: Only listed inventory objects used (office_chair_01, blanket_01, books_01).
No tape, adhesives, fasteners, or clamps used.
No permanent modifications made to any object.
No damage to any listed object.
No reliance on unknown liquid contents (spray bottles not used).
No reliance on electrical properties (power strip not used).
Object used as weight (books) has physical evidence of mass (hardcover/paperback books).

zero_initial_plan.title: Blanket edge stabilizer
zero_initial_plan.summary: Use books as a weight to hold down one edge of the blanket on the office chair seat, preventing it from shifting.

steps.action: Place a stack of books on the edge of the blanket resting on the office chair seat to prevent shifting.
steps.why_it_helps: Weight prevents blanket edge from moving on chair seat.

findings.claim: Weight of books prevents blanket edge from shifting on chair seat.
findings.explanation: The plan asserts that added weight stops movement, but no evidence shows sufficient friction between blanket and chair seat to prevent sliding; weight alone does not guarantee non‑slippage.
findings.recommended_fix: Demonstrate or add a mechanism to increase friction (e.g., rough surface) or verify that chair seat texture provides enough grip for the blanket edge when weighted.

zero_final_plan.title: Blanket edge stabilizer
zero_final_plan.summary: Use books as weight to hold the blanket edge down on the office chair seat, preventing shift.

steps.action: Place a stack of books on the blanket edge and fold the blanket edge over the books on the chair seat.

capability_uses.purpose: Secure edge over books to prevent shift

steps.why_it_helps: Weight holds the edge down, preventing it from sliding on the chair seat.

findings.claim: Weight holds blanket edge down, preventing slide.
findings.explanation: The plan assumes weight alone prevents sliding, but no evidence shows sufficient friction between blanket and chair seat to guarantee no shift.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a folded blanket layer under the edge to increase friction, or use books to create a small barrier that physically blocks movement.

findings.claim: Placing books on the blanket edge will prevent the blanket edge from shifting.
findings.explanation: The plan assumes the books will not slide off the blanket, but no friction or non‑slip property is established for the blanket or books.

findings.claim: Weight holds the edge down, preventing it from sliding on the chair seat.
findings.explanation: The books' provide_weight capability does not guarantee non‑slip or immobilization; sliding would defeat the goal.
